modelingNotes: Camp North End: 701 Keswick Avenue — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-cne-701-keswick.ts

One bay of the Army Quartermaster Corps' Building No. 5 (1941–43), cut free of its neighbours in the 2021 renovation: `clt-cne-201-camp-road` is the warehouse's north-east half, beyond a passage cut through it, and the parking garage and Kinship East stand on its south-west end. Shops and restaurants. A tall red-brick block 55 × 38 m with one corrugated-metal clerestory monitor across it and a slightly lower annex on the north-west side; north-east of it, on the slab of the bay removed for the passage, a low brick wing and a curved canopy.
Identity: the tall brick block with its single silver monitor, between 201 Camp Road and the garage.

Evidence: - OSM: the outline way/702547987 and its parts: the monitor way/835808943 (height 10.4), the roofs 835808944 and 1108280895 (8.2), the north-west annex 835808946 (8), the low wing relation/14759154 (4.2), the curved canopy 1109057437 (5.2, roof:shape round) and the slab 1109057438 (1). - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016, 1 m (measured, NAVD88): ground 227.9–228.7 (y = 0 is 227.9); deck 237.3 (9.4 m); the monitor 240.1 (12.2 m); the annex 236.4 (8.5 m). The flight predates the cut: it still shows the warehouse running on north-east over the passage, so the wing (4.2 m) and the canopy (5.2 m) take OSM's heights. - C-M Historic Landmarks Commission survey report (2017, landmarkscommission.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Ford-Motor-Co-Plant-SR.pdf), Buildings Nos. 4–6 (published): brick, 180 ft wide, corrugated-metal monitors across the width; No. 5 has ten. - Mecklenburg County tax parcel 07903C99: built 1943, face brick. Camp North End leasing brochure (2021, camp.nc): "701 Keswick Avenue", 38,000 sq ft, retail. - Photo (EVIDENCE): its end wall at the left of https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Free_Range_Brewing_Camp_North_End_in_the_301_Camp_building_Early_June_2025.jpg (City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0): orange-red brick, black-framed windows in two tiers, a storefront row and a row high in the wall. - USGS NAIP orthophoto (public domain): white roofs.

Estimated: window sizes and counts (from the one partial photo, applied to every face); the curved canopy's form (a barrel vault from OSM's roof:shape, springing at 3.6 m), its posts; the wing's walls.
Frame and kit: `clt-cne-301-camp-road.ts`. y along the long axis (bearing 39.67°), placement bearing 39.67; origin at the outline's centroid, lng −80.8333009, lat 35.2454296.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-cne-701-keswick", model "clt-cne-701-keswick"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-cne-701-keswick.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
